title: Career Roadmap · Maintenance Technician
summary: A Maintenance Technician helps keep electrical and electronic equipment operating safely and reliably. The work may include routine inspections, preventive maintenance, fault identification, component replacement, testing and maintenance documentation.

about.label: Industry
about.text: Manufacturing, electrical systems, industrial automation, utilities, facilities and infrastructure

about.label: Primary Workplaces
about.text: Factories, production plants, commercial buildings, power facilities, workshops and maintenance departments

about.label: Core Responsibility
about.text: Inspect, maintain, troubleshoot and repair electrical and electronic equipment to support safe, reliable operation

blocks.text: A Maintenance Technician helps keep electrical and electronic equipment operating safely and reliably. The work may include routine inspections, preventive maintenance, fault identification, component replacement, testing and maintenance documentation.

Depending on the employer, a technician may work with electric motors, control panels, sensors, pumps, generators, industrial machines, lighting systems, UPS units, batteries or automated production equipment.

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: An electrical maintenance technician focuses primarily on electrical equipment and associated controls. A mechanical maintenance technician focuses more on mechanical systems, while an instrumentation technician specialises in measurement instruments, process controls and calibration. In many workplaces, these responsibilities overlap.

Electrical maintenance work can involve dangerous voltages and stored energy. Live electrical work, isolation, testing and repairs must follow applicable safety rules and be performed only by trained, authorised personnel.

blocks.text: This roadmap follows a typical three-year diploma structure. The exact curriculum and workshop facilities vary by institution.
Year 1 — Electrical and Electronic Foundations

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Develop basic knowledge of circuits, components, measurements and safe working practices.
Core subjects:
Practical activities:

items.text: Identify resistors, capacitors, diodes and other basic components.
Assemble low-voltage training circuits under supervision.
Measure voltage, current and resistance using appropriate instruments.
Learn safe instrument handling and electrical hazard identification.

blocks.label: Year 1 outcome
blocks.text: Understand basic electrical circuits, electronic components, measurements and workshop safety.
Year 2 — Electrical Machines and Maintenance Fundamentals

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Understand the equipment commonly found in industrial and building maintenance environments.
Core subjects:
Practical activities:

items.text: Study motor nameplates and wiring diagrams.
Perform supervised continuity and resistance checks on de-energised training equipment.
Assemble a low-voltage control circuit on an approved training board.
Prepare an inspection checklist for a motor or electrical panel.
Learn how to record equipment faults and maintenance activities.

blocks.label: Year 2 outcome
blocks.text: Understand electrical machines, control circuits, protection devices and routine maintenance processes.
Year 3 — Industrial Maintenance and Troubleshooting

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Prepare for entry-level maintenance work in industrial or facilities environments.
Core subjects:

items.text: UPS, battery and backup power fundamentals

blocks.text: Practical activities:

items.text: Develop a fault-reporting workflow for a simulated electrical machine.
Interpret a motor-control circuit and identify its major components.
Create a preventive-maintenance schedule for sample equipment.
Use a low-voltage PLC training kit, where available.
Record sample inspection measurements and flag unusual readings.
Prepare a root-cause analysis for a fictional recurring equipment fault.

blocks.label: Year 3 outcome
blocks.text: Demonstrate maintenance fundamentals, equipment documentation, basic troubleshooting logic and readiness for supervised technical work.

rows.text: Measure voltage, resistance and other supported quantities
Assess insulation condition under approved procedures
Identify and verify likely failure causes
Record work orders, assets and maintenance history
Prepare inspection logs and maintenance reports
Identify selected abnormal heating patterns when properly trained
Support condition monitoring of rotating equipment

blocks.text: Instrument selection and testing procedures must match the equipment, measurement category, manufacturer instructions and workplace safety requirements.
Project 1 — Electrical Component Identification and Test Log
Beginner

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Learn to identify electrical components and organise test results.
Build:

items.text: A catalogue of common electrical and electronic components.
Basic circuit diagrams for low-voltage training circuits.
A component identification and rating table.
A report explaining the purpose and limitations of each test.

blocks.label: Skills demonstrated
blocks.text: Electrical fundamentals, component identification, measurement and documentation.
Project 2 — Motor Preventive-Maintenance Checklist
Intermediate

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Design a structured inspection and maintenance record for a sample electric motor.
Build:

items.text: A motor asset record with nameplate information.
An inspection checklist based on manufacturer guidance.
Fields for unusual noise, temperature observations and visible damage.
A record of authorised electrical test results.
A maintenance history and escalation section.

blocks.label: Skills demonstrated
blocks.text: Equipment inspection, maintenance planning, safety awareness and technical reporting.
Project 3 — Low-Voltage Motor Control Demonstrator
Advanced

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Demonstrate the relationship between control circuits and motor operation.
Build:

items.text: A start/stop control sequence using an approved training board.
A circuit diagram and component list.
A troubleshooting decision tree and test record.

blocks.label: Skills demonstrated
blocks.text: Control-circuit fundamentals, electrical diagrams, troubleshooting and systematic testing.
The project should use suitable educational equipment and instructor-approved voltage levels. Do not build or test an improvised mains-powered system.
Project 4 — Maintenance Tracking Dashboard
Capstone

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Demonstrate how maintenance teams track equipment health and recurring failures.
Build:

items.text: Preventive-maintenance due dates and work-order status.
A dashboard for downtime and recurring-fault trends.
A prioritisation system based on documented risk criteria.

blocks.label: Skills demonstrated
blocks.text: Maintenance planning, Excel, data analysis, record keeping and reliability awareness.
All practical electrical projects should be performed using appropriate training equipment, supervision, isolation procedures and protective measures.

After gaining experience, a maintenance technician can specialise in:

blocks.label: Industrial Electrical Maintenance
blocks.text: Motors, control panels and industrial electrical equipment.

blocks.label: Motor and Drive Maintenance
blocks.text: Motor starters, variable-frequency drives and related systems.

blocks.label: Electrical Panel Testing
blocks.text: Panel assembly, wiring verification and testing.

blocks.label: PLC and Automation Maintenance
blocks.text: Industrial controls, sensors and automated machinery.

blocks.label: Instrumentation Maintenance
blocks.text: Sensors, transmitters and measurement equipment.

blocks.label: Power Distribution Maintenance
blocks.text: Distribution systems and protective equipment, subject to authorisation.

blocks.label: UPS and Backup Power Systems
blocks.text: Battery systems, backup power and equipment checks.

blocks.label: Facilities Maintenance
blocks.text: Electrical systems in commercial and institutional buildings.

blocks.label: Condition Monitoring
blocks.text: Selected equipment-health indicators and maintenance trends.

blocks.label: Maintenance Planning
blocks.text: Work orders, preventive schedules, asset records and reliability reporting.

By the end of the diploma, the student should aim to have:

items.text: Strong knowledge of electrical and electronic fundamentals.
The ability to interpret basic electrical and control diagrams.
Practical exposure to electrical machines and motor-control circuits.
Familiarity with appropriate electrical test instruments.
Understanding of preventive maintenance and fault-reporting workflows.
Two or three practical maintenance or troubleshooting projects.
Workshop or industrial internship experience where available.
Evidence of safe working practices and accurate documentation.
A CV tailored to electrical maintenance trainee, maintenance technician or industrial maintenance roles.

blocks.text: The most practical route is to begin as an electrical maintenance trainee or maintenance technician, gain supervised experience with industrial equipment, and then specialise in automation, motor systems, instrumentation or facilities maintenance.

For employability, prioritise a maintenance case-study portfolio containing a motor inspection checklist, a sample control-circuit diagram, a structured fault-analysis report and a preventive-maintenance schedule. These deliverables demonstrate practical thinking, documentation discipline and an understanding of safe maintenance workflows.
